text:
Pyotr Kochetkov stopped all 24 shots he faced on Saturday night, and Carolina turned a quiet first period into a 4-0 win in St. Louis. Kochetkov, drafted 36th overall by the Hurricanes in 2019 out of Ryazan-VDV, saw only a few real tests. The best was a 21 percent look for Jake Neighbours in the third, and he turned it away. By our numbers he saved about two goals more than those 24 shots deserved, which is what a shutout looks like when the goalie is actually earning it.

The game turned in the second period. CAR was already slightly ahead on chance quality in the first, then took over, out-chancing STL 1.62 to 0.87 in expected goals (a measure of how dangerous each shot was). Sean Walker scored at 4:45, Jesperi Kotkaniemi answered his own team's lead by adding another 20 seconds later, and Logan Stankoven made it 3-0 at 13:35. Jackson Blake assisted on the first of those and reached 100 career points. Nikolaj Ehlers added a power-play goal early in the third, and Seth Jarvis had two assists.

The result was earned. CAR finished with 3.67 expected goals to STL's 2.11, and our simulations of every shot give the Hurricanes a 75 percent chance of deserving the win. Joel Hofer stopped 35 of 39 for STL and was close to par for the quality he faced, so the gap was in the skaters in front of him and the goalie at the other end. The facts we have don't include streaks or standings for either club, so we'll leave this as one lopsided night for CAR and a game STL will want to forget.
